title: Permutation in string
statement_markdown: Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return `True` if `s2` contains a permutation of `s1`, or `False` otherwise.
starter_code:

hints: Use a fixed-size sliding window of length `len(s1)`.
explanation: Count character frequencies in `s1`. Slide a window of size `len(s1)` across `s2` and check if the character frequencies in the window match those of `s1`.
reference_solution:
def check_inclusion(s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
    from collections import Counter
    if len(s1) > len(s2): return False
    s1_counts = Counter(s1)
    window_counts = Counter(s2[:len(s1)])
    if s1_counts == window_counts: return True
    for i in range(len(s1), len(s2)):
        window_counts[s2[i]] += 1
        window_counts[s2[i - len(s1)]] -= 1
        if window_counts[s2[i - len(s1)]] == 0:
            del window_counts[s2[i - len(s1)]]
        if s1_counts == window_counts:
            return True
    return False
